inspection_summary: Inspected all 329 normalized lines. The paper reports a rigorous finite verification of RH, sketches a certificate built from half-line sign changes plus Turing-style completeness accounting, explains validated-numerics and resolution/throughput choices, and traces how the enlarged certified height changes several explicit downstream bounds. Formula extraction is damaged in two localized layout blocks, but the surrounding prose supports the accepted mechanisms.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the work and summarizes the rigorously certified finite-height RH claim.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the finite verification height H, contrasts evidential standards of earlier computations, and states the main certified bound.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Theory and computation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sketches the sign-change and Turing-method certification architecture, validated-arithmetic implementation, resolution choice, and computational tradeoffs.

sections_inspected.label: 3 overview and 3.1 Bounds on primes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains H as a reusable input to explicit prime estimates and derives a finite range on which RH-conditional error bounds become unconditional.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2 Zero-free regions and zero density estimates
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Lists coupled dependencies of zero-free, reciprocal-growth, and zero-density estimates on H and a zero-free constant.

sections_inspected.label: 3.3 Oscillations in the prime number theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Describes upper- and lower-range consequences for first sign changes and warns that the incremental gain from larger H may be small.

sections_inspected.label: 3.4 The de Bruijn–Newman constant
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the constant in prose, relates its sign to RH, and transfers a tabulated H threshold into an improved upper bound while identifying the next unmet threshold.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-mathematical resource acknowledgements inspected for completeness.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography inspected; an interleaved footnote at lines 239–240 supplies a representation conversion for the de Bruijn–Newman threshold.

accepted_units.title: Finite RH verification as a bounded completeness claim
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns partial verification into a precise epistemic object: H is the greatest height through which every nontrivial zero is known to lie on the critical line. This separates a bounded certified claim from a proof of RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The abstract at lines 20–23 previews the paper's new value; historical comparisons begin at line 34.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low. The unit is supported by continuous prose; numeral superscripts are flattened but do not affect the definition of H.

accepted_units.title: Rigor and reproducibility distinguish the new finite-height theorem
accepted_units.why_material: The authors make accumulated rounding and truncation error part of the validity question, contrast this with computations lacking clear setup details, and state a rigorously supported height and zero count that also independently checks earlier ranges.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 34–51 provide the earlier-computation history, but page-layout footnotes split that passage; the accepted span starts at the complete rigor comparison and ends with the theorem's stated independent-verification consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate. Flattened powers of ten must be read as rendered scientific notation, but the prose and theorem statement are otherwise coherent.

accepted_units.title: Local sign witnesses plus global zero accounting certify a finite RH range
accepted_units.why_material: Sign changes of the completed zeta function witness critical-line zeros, while a variation of Turing's method checks that the expected total has been accounted for. The combination, rather than sign sampling alone, excludes missed off-line zeros in the range.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an outline that delegates algorithmic detail to the cited prior work; it supports the logical certificate shape, not an independently reproducible implementation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low. Continuous prose states both the local witness and global completeness roles.

accepted_units.title: Validated representation can improve memory locality without dropping rigor
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing full interval arithmetic with maintained ball arithmetic preserves a rigorous enclosure representation while roughly halving storage and improving cache friendliness, linking proof-grade numerics to systems-level feasibility.
accepted_units.context_note: The source gives two implementation reasons—maintenance status and representation size—but no benchmark isolating their individual effects.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low. The comparison is explicit in prose and does not depend on formulas.

accepted_units.title: Count only the zero information required by the certificate
accepted_units.why_material: The computation abandons high-precision zero isolation once a sign change is found, because the certification goal needs a count rather than a stored high-precision zero database. This is a reusable distinction between sufficient witnesses and unnecessarily rich outputs at scale.
accepted_units.context_note: The sentence ending at line 87 resumes at lines 96–97 after a displaced historical footnote and page markers at lines 88–95; those intervening lines are not evidence for this mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate. Page extraction interrupts the paragraph, but the main sentence reconnects unambiguously as 'moved on'; the reported sampling/isolation rate is legible.

accepted_units.title: Certification strength and sampling density trade directly against throughput
accepted_units.why_material: The source records hardware behavior, parameter retuning at greater height, total compute, and a comparison that attributes large speed differences to FFT use, sampling density, and multiprecision rigorous numerics. It exposes the cost structure behind a trustworthy large-scale certificate.
accepted_units.context_note: The hardware and historical runs are not controlled like-for-like experiments, so the figures support engineering diagnosis rather than universal causal ratios.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate. Several units and symbols are flattened, but the qualitative comparisons and stated attributions remain clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: A larger certified H propagates through explicit prime estimates
accepted_units.why_material: The section frames finite RH verification as a reusable starting parameter: estimates for prime-counting error terms and Bertrand-type intervals based on an older H can be confirmed or slightly improved when H increases.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed definitions at lines 125–127 are layout-damaged, but the named functions and the prose describing the transfer are recoverable; the precise formulas should be checked against a scan before formula-level reuse.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high for the displayed definitions, low for the source's qualitative H-dependence claim.

accepted_units.title: A finite RH certificate converts a global conditional estimate into a bounded unconditional result
accepted_units.why_material: The source states a condition relating the verified height H to x and applies the new H to obtain explicit finite ranges for three prime-counting error bounds. The mechanism demonstrates how finite zero information licenses conclusions far beyond the numerical verification height in a different variable.
accepted_units.context_note: The corollary is readable, but radical signs, exponents, and fraction layout are flattened; exact formula transcription requires later scan verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact constants and displayed inequalities; low for the prose-level transfer mechanism from a partial-RH height condition to a finite x-range.

accepted_units.title: Finite verification height interacts with other analytic constants
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes improvements driven directly by H from reciprocal-growth bounds that depend on both H and the zero-free constant R, and it identifies zero-density estimates as another consumer. This prevents treating one stronger certificate as the sole input to every downstream bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The zero-free-region display is spatially flattened, but the surrounding sentences state the roles of H and R explicitly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate for the exact zero-free-region formula; low for the dependency structure.

accepted_units.title: A stronger H can tighten first-sign-change bounds while yielding only marginal practical gain
accepted_units.why_material: The paper connects finite RH verification to both upper and lower exclusions for first sign changes, then explicitly notes diminishing returns because unconditional and RH-contingent bounds are already close. This is a useful limit on interpreting downstream fertility from a larger H.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 192–197 contain a page break; lines 198–201 complete the subsection by giving the lower-range computational consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate. Inequalities and powers are flattened, but the direction of both exclusions and the small-gain qualification are clear.

accepted_units.title: Crossing a published H threshold improves the de Bruijn–Newman upper bound
accepted_units.why_material: The prose defines the threshold role of Λ, states its equivalence to RH, and uses H greater than a specified cutoff to move an upper bound from 0.22 to 0.2. It also identifies the next threshold as unmet and distinguishes a certified corollary from speculative extra decimals.
accepted_units.context_note: The defining transform at lines 204–211 is extraction-defective and is not used as unit evidence. A displaced footnote at lines 239–240 explains that the cited table's X equals 2H.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the threshold implication and stated corollary; high for the excluded defining formula, which requires scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A finite RH computation is a layered completeness certificate
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A trustworthy bounded RH result composes validated function evaluation, local critical-line zero witnesses, and a global expected-zero count; because the theorem needs completeness rather than a zero database, excess localization precision can be discarded without weakening that certificate shape.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper only outlines the inherited algorithm, so the exact truncation bounds, interval propagation, and Turing-method implementation are not established by this source span alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Computational rigor has a visible systems cost structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Representation size, cache behavior, target output precision, sampling density, FFT use, and multiprecision enclosures jointly determine whether a proof-grade computation scales; semantic sufficiency can recover resources that rigor itself consumes.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The historical throughput figures use different machines, algorithms, and sampling policies, so they do not isolate causal effects or supply portable performance ratios.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Certified height is a reusable but nonuniform downstream resource
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Increasing H can enlarge unconditional finite ranges, improve constants, or cross a discrete threshold in later results, but its utility depends on other analytic inputs and may be slight when competing unconditional bounds are already close.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several improvements are only stated as possible or slight and are not recalculated here; only the displayed prime-range corollary and Λ ≤ 0.2 are explicitly instantiated in this paper.

within_source_saturation: Saturated after inspecting every line: the certificate target, evidential standard, computational architecture, engineering tradeoffs, and each distinct downstream transfer mechanism are represented. Further units would chiefly duplicate the abstract/main theorem, split short lists of prospective improvements without additional mechanism, select non-controlled hardware detail in isolation, or rely on formula-defective displays and bibliography.
